recall.minute: Monte Carlo methods estimate values by averaging sampled returns over complete episodes, needing no model and not bootstrapping; they apply to episodic tasks and update after episodes end. First-visit MC averages returns after the first visit to a state per episode; every-visit uses all visits; both converge. In a five-state grid world (moves −1, exit D +10, exit A −10, γ = 1) four episodes give V(A) = −10, V(B) = 8, V(C) = 4, V(D) = 10, V(E) = −2; B and E differ though both lead to C, because MC learns each state from its own episodes. Updates can be incremental (1/N) or constant-α. MC control estimates Q(s, a) and improves greedily within GPI, maintaining exploration by exploring starts or ε-soft policies (π(a|s) ≥ ε/|A|), which converge to the best ε-soft policy. Off-policy methods learn a target π from behaviour b with coverage, using ratios Π π/b in which the dynamics cancel: ordinary IS is unbiased but high-variance; weighted IS is biased but preferred. Blackjack (200 states, γ = 1) is easy to simulate but hard to model, and MC control recovers near basic strategy.
